notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes to give you yet. My first attempt to fetch the sources failed with a message saying I had no tool calls left for this turn, and a test call I made just after got the same error. I couldn't read any page from enduringword.com, studylight.org, preceptaustin.org, netbible.org or the other sites on your list.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, because none of them would be backed by a source.

**Next step:** if you send the request again in a new turn, the tool should be available. I'd start with these pages:

- **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word on Isaiah 55, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages on Isaiah 55 at StudyLight or BibleHub, and Precept Austin's Isaiah 55 commentary.
- **Where Protestant traditions may differ:** I'd search the tradition sites for passages likely to divide them. These are guesses to check, not findings:
  - v. 3, the "everlasting covenant" with David, and how it links to Acts 13:34
  - v. 6, "while He may be found," and what it implies about the timing of grace
  - v. 11, God's word not returning empty, and whether it always achieves its aim or works through the means of grace
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on Isaiah 55, then BibleOdyssey, New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA. I'd also check GotQuestions and similar sites for how popular teaching uses v. 11 ("My word… will not return empty").

Alternatively, you can paste in the text of any of these pages and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes from that, citing each point.
